These routes of the platform API come from its [OpenAPI document](../openapi.json); [The REST API as a contract](../rest-api.md) says what Lakana promises about them.

## `POST /api/v1/environments/{environment_name}/connections`

Create a connection

From the web interface it needs a passkey touch within the last 15 minutes (403 `StepUpRequired`); a token never does.

Creates a connection of the environment: its kind, address and settings, and its secret, either new values (stored as a new secret `<name>-connection`, or the next free `<name>-connection-N` when a secret holds that name, born bound to it, never shown again) or the name of an existing secret. Needs `MANAGE_CONNECTION` in the environment, checked before anything in the body; naming a secret that is not bound to this connection also needs `MANAGE_SECRET`. Answers 403 without the right, 404 when the environment or the named secret does not exist, 409 when the name is taken (or every secret name up to `<name>-connection-100` is), and 422 for a name, kind, address, settings or secret keys that are not valid, naming the field. Answers 500 when the instance has no secrets master key.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `environment_name` | path | yes | text | The environment. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Request body (application/json, required): `ConnectionCreate`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | text | yes |  |
| `kind` | one of `postgresql`, `mariadb`, `sqlite-file`, `http`, `s3`, `gcs`, `azure`, `directory`, `tcp` | yes | The kind of source. |
| `address` | mapping of text to any | yes |  |
| `settings` | mapping of text to any | no |  |
| `secret` | text or null | no |  |
| `secret_values` | mapping of text to text (password) or null | no |  |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `201` | Successful Response | `ConnectionOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `409` | The request conflicts with the current state; the message says what to change. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

## `GET /api/v1/environments/{environment_name}/connections`

List the connections of an environment

Lists one page of connections, newest first, with the assets that declare each, its last test and what you may do with it (`actions`). Needs `READ_ENVIRONMENT` in the environment; a task token is refused with 403. Every reader gets the last test's `state`, `outcome` and `finished_at`; its `id`, `created_at`, `message` and `requested_by` only a holder of `MANAGE_CONNECTION` in the environment, and for anyone else those keys are absent. `sort` and `order` order the list by another field; one state is ordered by name. Answers 404 when the environment does not exist and 422 for an unknown `sort` or `order` or a cursor this list did not issue in this order.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `environment_name` | path | yes | text | The environment. |
| `limit` | query | no | whole number | Most connections returned (1 to 200). |
| `cursor` | query | no | text or null | The `next_cursor` of the previous page. |
| `sort` | query | no | text or null | What the list is sorted by: `created` (the default), `name` (in any letter case) or `status`, the last test: failed first, then queued or running, then passed, never tested last; one state by name. |
| `order` | query | no | text or null | `asc` or `desc`; by default `desc` for `created` (the newest first), `asc` for the others. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Successful Response | `ConnectionPage` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `ConnectionPage`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | list of `ConnectionOut` | yes |  |
| `next_cursor` | text or null | yes |  |

## `GET /api/v1/environments/{environment_name}/connections/{connection_name}`

Show a connection

Shows its address, settings (a CA certificate as its SHA-256 fingerprint), the name of its secret, the assets that declare it, its last test and what you may do with it (`actions`). Needs `READ_ENVIRONMENT` in the environment; a task token is refused with 403, naming no connection. Every reader gets the last test's `state`, `outcome` and `finished_at`; its `id`, `created_at`, `message` and `requested_by` only a holder of `MANAGE_CONNECTION` in the environment, and for anyone else those keys are absent. Answers 404 when the environment or the connection does not exist; the answer names no other connection.

## `PATCH /api/v1/environments/{environment_name}/connections/{connection_name}`

Change a connection

From the web interface it needs a passkey touch within the last 15 minutes (403 `StepUpRequired`); a token never does.

Changes its address, settings or secret; its name and kind never change. New secret values set its own secret again (or create the next free `<name>-connection`); `clear` with `secret` stops using the secret and unbinds it. Needs `MANAGE_CONNECTION` in the environment, and also `MANAGE_SECRET` to name a secret not bound to it, or for a change that could send its secret somewhere new (its address, a weaker TLS, another CA certificate, another way of sending it) without new values. Answers 403 without the rights, 404 when the environment, the connection or the named secret does not exist, 409 when every secret name up to `<name>-connection-100` is taken or the connection changed at the same time, and 422 when nothing is given or the result is not valid, naming the field.

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `environment_name` | path | yes | text | The environment. |
| `connection_name` | path | yes | text | The connection's name. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Request body (application/json, required): `ConnectionUpdate`

| `secret` | text or null | no |  |
| `secret_values` | mapping of text to text (password) or null | no |  |
| `clear` | list of text | no |  |

## `DELETE /api/v1/environments/{environment_name}/connections/{connection_name}`

Delete a connection

Deletes it and unbinds its secret, which stays in the environment. Needs `MANAGE_CONNECTION` in the environment. Answers 404 when the environment or the connection does not exist, and 409, naming a declaring asset, while a deployed project version declares it: deploy a version without it first.

## `POST /api/v1/environments/{environment_name}/connections/{connection_name}/tests`

Queue a test of a connection

A worker checks that the connection's host can be reached with its settings and secret and records an outcome; poll the test with `GET .../tests/{test_id}`. Needs `MANAGE_CONNECTION` in the environment. Answers 404 when the environment or the connection does not exist and 409, naming the open test, while a test of the connection that is under 10 minutes old is queued or running; an older open test is finished as failed first.

## `GET /api/v1/connections`

List the connections of every environment you may read

Without `environment`, lists one page of the connections of every environment where you hold `READ_ENVIRONMENT`, newest first over all of them; each names its `environment`. An environment where you do not hold it is left out, so this is never a 404, and never a 403 but for a task token, which is refused as every connection read is. With `environment`, it answers exactly what `GET /api/v1/environments/{environment_name}/connections` answers, with its 403 and 404. Each connection carries its last test and what you may do with it (`actions`), as in that list: the last test's `id`, `created_at`, `message` and `requested_by` only where you hold `MANAGE_CONNECTION`, and absent elsewhere. `sort` and `order` order the list as on the list of one environment. Send `next_cursor` back as `cursor` with the same sort for the next page; a cursor of the list of one environment or of another order is refused with 422 here.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | query | no | text or null | Only this environment. |
| `limit` | query | no | whole number | Most connections returned (1 to 200). |
| `cursor` | query | no | text or null | The `next_cursor` of the previous page. |
| `sort` | query | no | text or null | What the list is sorted by: `created` (the default), `name` (in any letter case) or `status`, the last test: failed first, then queued or running, then passed, never tested last; one state by name. |
| `order` | query | no | text or null | `asc` or `desc`; by default `desc` for `created` (the newest first), `asc` for the others. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Successful Response | `ConnectionPage` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `ConnectionPage`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | list of `ConnectionOut` | yes |  |
| `next_cursor` | text or null | yes |  |

## `GET /api/v1/connections/environments`

List the environments whose connections you may read, and what you may do there

Every environment where you hold `READ_ENVIRONMENT`, sorted by name, with its `actions`: `create` and `test` where you hold `MANAGE_CONNECTION`, and `name_secret` (naming an existing secret for a connection) where you hold `MANAGE_SECRET` too. Empty when there is none. A task token is refused with 403, as every connection read is.

## `POST /api/v1/environments/{environment_name}/connection-tests`

Queue a test of every connection of an environment (Test all), a page at a time

Takes one page of the environment's connection list, newest first (`limit` 1 to 200, default 200), and handles each connection in turn: a connection whose test is queued or running and under 10 minutes old is not queued again, and that test is returned with `queued: false`; an older open test is finished as failed first; every other connection gets a new test with `queued: true`. An open test is never a 409. Poll each test with `GET .../connections/{connection}/tests/{test_id}`, and send `next_cursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it takes the cursors of `GET /api/v1/environments/{environment_name}/connections` and refuses others with 422. Needs `MANAGE_CONNECTION` in the environment, as a single test does. Answers 404 when the environment does not exist, and 409 when a connection changed at the same time: the connections before it stay queued, and sending the request again returns their tests with `queued: false`.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `environment_name` | path | yes | text | The environment. |
| `limit` | query | no | whole number | Most connections tested (1 to 200). |
| `cursor` | query | no | text or null | The `next_cursor` of the previous page. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `202` | Successful Response | `ConnectionQueuedTestPage` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `409` | The request conflicts with the current state; the message says what to change. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `ConnectionQueuedTestPage`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | list of `ConnectionQueuedTestOut` | yes |  |
| `next_cursor` | text or null | yes |  |

## `GET /api/v1/tasks/self/connections/{name}`

Fetch a connection the running task's asset declares, with its secret

For the helpers of `lakana.ingest` inside a Lakana task; nothing else needs it. Answers only the task's own token while its attempt runs, for a connection its deployed asset declares in `@asset(connections=[...])`, in the task's environment. Every call is in the audit log: `CONNECTION_CREDENTIAL_FETCHED` (committed before the answer is sent) or `CONNECTION_CREDENTIAL_REFUSED`. Answers 403 with "only a running task can fetch a connection" for any other token, "connection `NAME` is not declared by asset `ASSET`" for a name the asset does not declare (whether or not a connection of that name exists), and "connection `NAME` is not in environment `ENV`" for a declared name the environment lacks; 401 for a token whose attempt has ended or was claimed again. The answer is never cached (`Cache-Control: no-store`, `Pragma: no-cache`).

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | path | yes | text | The connection's name. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Successful Response | `TaskConnectionOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `TaskConnectionOut`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | text | yes |  |
| `kind` | text | yes |  |
| `address` | mapping of text to any | yes |  |
| `settings` | mapping of text to any | yes |  |
| `endpoints` | list of `EndpointOut` | yes |  |
| `secret` | mapping of text to text or null | yes |  |
